title: Jason: The Quest for the Fleece
subtitle: A one-sandalled man, a usurper's trap, and the finest crew ever rowed

learningObjectives.text: Why does Pelias send Jason for the Golden Fleece?

main.author: Apollonius Rhodius
main.locator: Argonautica 1, Pelias' commission and Jason's sign; Book 1, normalized characters 79-962
main.excerpt: who, at the behest of King Pelias, down through the mouth of Pontus and between the Cyanean rocks, sped well-benched Argo in quest of the golden fleece. Such was the oracle that Pelias heard, that a hateful doom awaited him to be slain at the prompting of the man whom he should see coming forth from the people with but one sandal. And no long time after, in accordance with that true report, Jason crossed the stream of wintry Anaurus on foot, and saved one sandal from the mire, but the other he left in the depths held back by the flood. And straightway he came to Pelias to share the banquet which the king was offering to his father Poseidon and the rest of the gods, though he paid no honour to Pelasgian Hera. Quickly the king saw him and pondered, and devised for him the toil of a troublous voyage, in order that on the sea or among strangers he might lose his home-return.

narrativeBlocks.title: The prophecy of one sandal
narrativeBlocks.body: Pelias seized the throne of Iolcus from Jason's father — and an oracle warned him to beware a man wearing a single sandal. When Jason walks into court having lost a sandal helping an old woman (the goddess Hera in disguise) across a river, Pelias knows the prophecy has arrived.

narrativeBlocks.title: A quest designed to kill
narrativeBlocks.body: Pelias cannot murder the stranger at his own hearth, so he offers a 'noble' deal: bring back the Golden Fleece from distant Colchis, and the throne is yours. It is meant to be a death sentence — no one has ever survived the voyage east.

narrativeBlocks.title: The Argo and her crew
narrativeBlocks.body: Jason answers by building the greatest ship Greece has seen — the Argo — and recruiting heroes to fill her: Heracles, Orpheus the singer, the twins Castor and Pollux, swift Atalanta. Fifty oars of legend rowing one doomed errand.

narrativeBlocks.title: Why the fleece matters
narrativeBlocks.body: The fleece is more than treasure: it is the golden ram that carried Jason's kin to safety generations ago. Reclaiming it would be both a heroic feat and a dynastic claim — which is exactly why Pelias hopes it never comes back.

narrativeBlocks.title: A different kind of hero
narrativeBlocks.body: Jason is not Achilles or Heracles — his gift is not strength but gathering: assembling the right people and letting them shine. Watch how often the quest succeeds through OTHERS, not Jason himself.

quiz.prompt: Why does Pelias send Jason after the Golden Fleece?

choices.text: The fleece is needed to cure a plague
Jason volunteered to prove his courage
An oracle warned him of a one-sandalled man — the quest is a death sentence designed to remove the claimant
The gods commanded it at Delphi

quiz.explanation: Pelias wants rid of the prophesied threat; Colchis is meant to kill him.

quiz.prompt: What makes the Argo's crew remarkable?

choices.text: They are all sons of kings
They are volunteers seeking the fleece's magic
The gods chose each by lot
It gathers the greatest heroes of the age — Heracles, Orpheus, Castor and Pollux, Atalanta — Jason's real gift is assembling them

quiz.explanation: The Argo carries an all-star crew; the quest succeeds through collective heroism, not Jason's strength.
